territorial_scope.description: Applies to electric companies and retail electricity consumers in Oregon, through amendments to ORS chapter 757.

evidence.quote: Sections 2 and 5 of this 2025 Act are added to and made a part of ORS chapter 757.

summary.short: Oregon HB 3546 (2025) adds ORS chapter 757 provisions requiring the Public Utility Commission to set a separate rate class and tariff for large energy use facilities (20 MW or more) and requiring electric companies to contract with them for 10 years or longer. Effective on passage.
summary.long: Oregon HB 3546 (2025) adds Sections 2 and 5 to ORS chapter 757. A large energy use facility is a facility, under common ownership or control, that uses or can use 20 megawatts or more and is primarily engaged in a service under NAICS code 518210 (2022). The Public Utility Commission must create a separate classification of service and tariff schedule for these retail electricity consumers. The tariff must allocate or directly assign the costs of serving the class and mitigate the risk of unwarranted cost shifts to other consumers; the Commission must weigh listed criteria when approving tariffs. Electric companies must contract with these consumers for 10 years or longer, with a minimum payment obligation and a possible excess-demand charge, and must notify consumers of delays within their reasonable control. Section 6 applies the contract rules to contracts made on or after the effective date and to earlier contracts that require significant new investment. Section 3 provides that neither party must use the classification until a tariff is approved; Section 3 is repealed January 2, 2028. Section 7 requires a Commission report to interim energy committees by September 1 of each even-numbered year; Section 7 is repealed January 2, 2035. Direct access, green power rates and special contracts are preserved. The Act takes effect on passage as an emergency measure.

notes: Text is the enrolled version (HB 3546-B). The governor's approval date and filing date are blank in the document, and the Act takes effect on passage (Sec. 9, emergency clause); the passage date is not stated, so the effective date used in Sec. 6 cannot be fixed from the text. Sec. 3 is repealed on January 2, 2028 (Sec. 4), and Sec. 7 (the reporting duty) is repealed on January 2, 2035 (Sec. 8). Sec. 3 says parties are not required to use the classification if no tariff has been approved, while Sec. 5(1)(a) says the Commission 'shall require' contracts; the text does not reconcile these. Internal cross-references (e.g., Sec. 2(2)(b) to Sec. 5(1)(b)(A)(v)) are not coded as relations. Relation target IDs are blank because no registry IDs for ORS chapters were supplied.

obligations.summary: Public Utility Commission must provide a separate classification of service with its own tariff schedule for retail electricity consumers that are large energy use facilities. Any such tariff must allocate or directly assign costs, meet the contract conditions under Section 5(1)(b)(A)(v), and mitigate cost-shifting risks. In approving a proposed tariff, the Commission must consider the rate factors listed in Section 2(3).

enforcement.note: The text contains no fine, penalty, criminal sanction, licence revocation, benefit clawback, suspension or blocking provision. Sections 1-9 direct the Public Utility Commission to create a tariff class and require contracts, a delay notice and a report. Section 1 adds Sections 2 and 5 to ORS chapter 757, but any enforcement provisions in that chapter are not in this document.
